question: A MELD score of ≥15 is the threshold above which the mortality benefit of liver transplantation exceeds the risk of the procedure, making transplant listing appropriate.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. MELD ≥15 is the widely accepted threshold for transplant listing; below this, medical management carries lower mortality than the transplant procedure itself. MELD incorporates creatinine, bilirubin, and INR.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. MELD ≥15 marks the point at which transplant-related mortality is outweighed by the survival benefit — a MELD below 15 means the patient is likely to do better on medical management than on the transplant waiting list.
